5.1 Oils and Fats

5.1 Oils and Fats

5.1

Oils and Fats

油與脂肪

structuresaturationmelting pointhydrogenation
5.1 Oils and Fats

Formation of Oils and Fats

Oils and fats are naturally occurring esters（酯類）. Most oils and fats are triglycerides（三酸甘油酯）.

A triglyceride is formed when one glycerol（甘油） molecule reacts with three fatty acid（脂肪酸） molecules.

In the general formula, R represents a long hydrocarbon chain（碳氫鏈）.

The reaction is called esterification（酯化反應）.

TEACHER HINT
Key words: esters, triglycerides, glycerol, fatty acids, hydrocarbon chain, esterification.
5.1 Oils and Fats

Triglyceride Formation

Glycerol+3 Fatty Acids→Triglyceride+3H₂O

Glycerol is also called propan-1,2,3-triol（丙烷-1,2,3-三醇）. It contains three hydroxyl groups（羥基） and forms three ester linkages（酯鍵）.

5.1 Oils and Fats

Saturated vs Unsaturated Fatty Acids

TEACHER HINT
Saturated: only single bonds. Unsaturated: at least one double bond.
5.1 Oils and Fats

Saturated vs Unsaturated: Comparison

AspectSaturated Fatty Acid 飽和Unsaturated Fatty Acid 不飽和
Carbon–carbon bondsOnly single bonds（單鍵）At least one double bond（雙鍵）
ShapestraightBent or kinked（彎折的）
Packingmore closelyDo not pack as closely
Attractionstronger（較強）weaker（較弱）
Melting pointhigherlower
Typical statesolidliquid
5.1 Oils and Fats

Oils and Fats: Comparison

AspectOils 油Fats 脂肪
State at room temperatureUsually liquidUsually solid or semi-solid
Main fatty acidsMore unsaturated fatty acids（不飽和脂肪酸）More saturated fatty acids（飽和脂肪酸）
Melting pointlowerhigher
ExamplesOlive oil, soybean oil, corn oilButter, ghee, animal fat
Common Mistake
Palm oil and coconut oil are plant products with relatively high proportions of saturated fatty acids（飽和脂肪酸）. Fish oils can contain high proportions of unsaturated fatty acids（不飽和脂肪酸）.
5.1 Oils and Fats

Visual Link: Oil and Fat

Oil usually has a lower melting point; fat usually has a higher melting point.

The difference is related to molecular shape, packing and intermolecular attractions（分子間作用力）.

5.1 Oils and Fats

Why Oils Are Usually Liquid

1. Double bond
Unsaturated chains contain carbon–carbon double bonds（雙鍵）. A cis double bond（順式雙鍵） bends the chain.
2. Packing
Bent molecules cannot pack closely.
3. Attraction
Intermolecular attractions（分子間作用力） are weaker.
4. Melting point
Less thermal energy（熱能） is required, so melting point is lower.

Saturated chains are straighter and have higher melting points.

5.1 Oils and Fats

Hydrogenation

Hydrogenation is an addition reaction（加成反應） in which hydrogen is added across carbon–carbon double bonds.
Conditions / 條件
  • hydrogen gas（氫氣）, H₂
  • a nickel catalyst（鎳催化劑）
  • about 180°C
Industrial Use
Converts liquid vegetable oils（液態植物油） into semi-solid products such as margarine（人造奶油）.
5.1 Oils and Fats

Hydrogenation: Bond Change

5.1 Oils and Fats

Changes During Hydrogenation

  1. The number of carbon–carbon double bonds decreases.
  2. The degree of saturation（飽和程度） increases.
  3. The chains become straighter and pack more closely.
  4. Intermolecular attractions become stronger.
  5. The melting point increases.
  6. The product becomes more solid at room temperature.
5.1 Oils and Fats

Worked Example: Hydrogenation

QUESTION

Vegetable oil is reacted with hydrogen at 180°C in the presence of nickel. Explain why the product is more solid at room temperature.

Hydrogen adds across the carbon–carbon double bonds.
The oil becomes more saturated and the chains become straighter.
Molecules pack more closely, producing stronger intermolecular attractions.
The melting point increases, so the product is more solid.
TEACHER HINT
Expected chain: fewer C=C → straighter chains → closer packing → stronger attractions → higher melting point.
5.2 Cleaning Agents

5.2 Cleaning Agents

5.2

Cleaning Agents

清潔劑

soapsaponificationmicelleshard water
5.2 Cleaning Agents

Soap

Soap is a sodium or potassium salt（鹽） of a long-chain fatty acid.
RCOO−
Sodium soap
Example: sodium stearate（硬脂酸鈉）, C₁₇H₃₅COONa.
Usually harder → solid soap bars.
Potassium soap
Example: potassium palmitate（棕櫚酸鉀）, C₁₅H₃₁COOK.
Usually softer → liquid or soft soap.
5.2 Cleaning Agents

Saponification

Saponification is the alkaline hydrolysis（鹼性水解） of an oil or fat to produce soap and glycerol（甘油）.
Triglyceride + 3NaOH → Glycerol + 3RCOONa
5.2 Cleaning Agents

Laboratory Preparation of Soap

  1. Mix vegetable oil with concentrated sodium hydroxide（濃氫氧化鈉） solution.
  2. Heat while stirring carefully.
  3. Add saturated sodium chloride（飽和氯化鈉） solution.
  4. Allow the mixture to cool.
  5. Filter the solid soap.
  6. Wash with cold distilled water（蒸餾水）.
  7. Press and dry the soap.
5.2 Cleaning Agents

Salting Out

Soap dissolved in mixture
＋ saturated NaCl
Lower soap solubility
→
Solid soap separates
Key Point
Sodium chloride reduces the solubility of soap in water. This process is called salting out（鹽析）.
5.2 Cleaning Agents

Detergents

Detergents are synthetic cleaning agents（合成清潔劑）.
Common anions
alkylbenzene sulphonates（烷基苯磺酸鹽）
RSO₃⁻

alkyl sulphates（烷基硫酸鹽）
ROSO₃⁻
Source
Commonly manufactured from petroleum-derived raw materials（石油衍生原料）.
5.2 Cleaning Agents

Structure of a Cleaning-Agent Anion

Hydrophobic hydrocarbon tail疏水性碳氫尾部 · attracted to oil and grease
−Hydrophilic ionic head親水性離子頭部 · attracted to water
R—COO−
5.2 Cleaning Agents

Micelle Formation

5.2 Cleaning Agents

Cleansing Action: Stages 1–4

  1. Soap or detergent lowers the surface tension（表面張力） of water.
  2. The hydrophobic tails dissolve in the grease.
  3. The hydrophilic heads remain in the surrounding water.
  4. Agitation（攪動） breaks grease into smaller droplets.
5.2 Cleaning Agents

Cleansing Action: Stages 5–7

  1. Cleaning-agent anions surround each grease droplet to form a micelle（膠束）.
  2. The similarly charged heads repel one another and prevent recombination.
  3. The suspended droplets are removed during rinsing（沖洗）.
SPM Tip
Mention tail, head, agitation, micelle and rinsing. “Soap removes grease” alone is not enough.
5.2 Cleaning Agents

Soap in Hard Water

Hard water contains calcium ions（鈣離子）, Ca²⁺, and magnesium ions（鎂離子）, Mg²⁺.
2RCOO⁻ + Ca²⁺ → (RCOO)₂Ca(s)
2RCOO⁻ + Mg²⁺ → (RCOO)₂Mg(s)

Soap forms insoluble salts（不溶性鹽） called scum（皂垢）.

Scum wastes soap, reduces lather formation（泡沫形成） and leaves deposits. Detergent remains effective.

5.2 Cleaning Agents

Soap in Acidic Water

RCOO⁻+H⁺→RCOOH(s)

Soap anions react with hydrogen ions（氫離子） to form insoluble fatty acids.

Therefore, soap is less effective in acidic water. Detergents generally remain effective under acidic conditions（酸性條件）.

5.2 Cleaning Agents

Soap vs Detergent

AspectSoap 肥皂Detergent 合成清潔劑
Raw materialOils and fats（油與脂肪）Usually petroleum-derived
Functional groupCarboxylate（羧酸根） −COO⁻Sulphonate or sulphate（磺酸根或硫酸根）
Soft waterEffectiveEffective
Hard waterForms scum; less effectiveDoes not normally form scum
Acidic waterForms insoluble fatty acidGenerally effective
BiodegradabilityUsually biodegradable（可生物分解）Depends on structure
5.2 Cleaning Agents

Worked Example: Hard Water

QUESTION

Explain why detergent is more effective than soap in hard water.

Hard water contains Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions.
Soap anions form insoluble salts called scum.
Scum reduces the amount of soap available for cleansing.
Detergent anions do not normally form insoluble precipitates, so detergent remains effective.

5.3 Food Additives

Definition of Food Additives

Food additives are substances deliberately added（刻意加入） to food to preserve it or improve its taste, smell, appearance, texture or stability（穩定性）.
5.3 Food Additives

Main Types of Food Additives I

TypeFunctionExamples
Preservative 防腐劑Prevents or slows microbial growth; delays spoilageSalt, sugar, vinegar, sodium benzoate
Antioxidant 抗氧化劑Slows oxidation; delays rancidityAscorbic acid, tocopherol, BHA, BHT
Flavouring agent 調味劑Improves taste and smellMSG, vanilla essence, esters
Colouring agent 著色劑Improves colour and appearanceCaramel, chlorophyll, turmeric
5.3 Food Additives

Main Types of Food Additives II

TypeFunctionExamples
Emulsifier 乳化劑Helps two immiscible liquids（互不相溶液體） form an emulsionLecithin, mono- and diglycerides
Stabiliser 穩定劑Maintains a uniform mixtureLecithin, gelatin, gums
Thickener 增稠劑Increases viscosity（黏度） or forms a gelPectin, gelatin, starch
5.3 Food Additives

Important Examples I

Ascorbic acid 維生素 C
An antioxidant. It reacts with oxygen first and delays oxidation of the food.
Lecithin 卵磷脂
An emulsifier and stabiliser. It helps an oil–water mixture remain uniform.
5.3 Food Additives

Important Examples II

Pectin 果膠
A thickener that absorbs water and forms a gel（凝膠）.
Sodium benzoate 苯甲酸鈉
A preservative used in acidic foods and drinks to inhibit microbial growth（微生物生長）.
5.3 Food Additives

Food Product Matching

Pickled foods
preservatives
Jelly
thickener
Ice cream
prevents separating
5.3 Food Additives

Responsible Use of Food Additives

Permitted limits
Food additives must be used within permitted limits（允許限量）. Excessive intake may affect sensitive individuals（敏感人士）.
Do not hide poor quality
Food additives must not be used to hide spoilage, contamination or poor-quality ingredients.
SPM answering technique
Name the additive and link its function to the actual food product.

5.4 Medicines and Cosmetics

Medicines

Medicines are chemicals used to prevent, control or treat diseases and their symptoms.
Traditional medicines
Obtained mainly from natural sources（天然來源）.
Modern medicines
Manufactured and tested medicines used for defined medical purposes.

Natural origin does not automatically mean safe. Dosage, purity, interactions and contamination（污染） must be considered.

5.4 Medicines and Cosmetics

Traditional Medicines

SourceCommon Traditional Use
Aloe vera 蘆薈Minor skin irritation and mild burns
Ginger 薑nausea and digestive discomfort
Garlic 大蒜Supports general health
Turmeric 薑黃Minor skin conditions and inflammation
Ginseng 人參Improves energy and well-being
5.4 Medicines and Cosmetics

Analgesics

Analgesics（止痛藥） relieve pain without necessarily curing the underlying disease.
Aspirin
Relieves pain, fever and inflammation. May irritate the stomach lining（胃壁） and increase bleeding.
Paracetamol
Relieves pain and reduces fever. An overdose（過量服用） may cause severe liver damage.
Codeine
Stronger analgesic; may cause drowsiness, dependence or addiction.
5.4 Medicines and Cosmetics

Antibiotics

Antibiotics（抗生素） kill bacteria or inhibit their growth. They treat bacterial infections, not viral infections.
Stop treatment early
some bacteria remain alive
less susceptible bacteria（較不敏感的細菌） survive
survivors reproduce
more resistant bacteria（抗藥性細菌）
infection is harder to treat
TEACHER HINT
Do not say bacteria “decide to mutate”. Antibiotics select less-susceptible bacteria already present.
5.4 Medicines and Cosmetics

Psychotherapeutic Medicines

TypeFunctionExamples
Stimulant 興奮劑Increases activity and alertnessAmphetamine, methylphenidate
Antidepressant 抗抑鬱藥Treats symptoms of depressionImipramine, amitriptyline
Antipsychotic 抗精神病藥Treats disturbed thoughts or perceptionClozapine, haloperidol
5.4 Medicines and Cosmetics

Correct Use of Medicines

  • Follow the prescribed dosage（劑量） and schedule.
  • Read the label and instructions carefully.
  • Do not share prescription medicines.
  • Do not use expired medicines.
  • Inform the doctor about allergies and other medicines.
  • Complete a prescribed antibiotic course.
  • Seek advice if serious side effects（副作用） occur.
5.4 Medicines and Cosmetics

Cosmetics

Cosmetics are products used externally to clean, protect or beautify the body.
5.4 Medicines and Cosmetics

Basic Cosmetic Ingredients

IngredientFunctionExample
WaterActs as a solvent or continuous phasePurified water
Dye / pigmentProvides colourIron oxides
PreservativePrevents microbial growth and spoilagePermitted preservatives
Moisturiser / humectantRetains moistureGlycerol
FragranceProvides pleasant smellEssential oils
ThickenerIncreases viscosity（黏度）Xanthan gum
EmulsifierMixes oil and waterLecithin
5.4 Medicines and Cosmetics

Harmful or Prohibited Ingredients

mercury compounds（汞化合物）kidney and nervous-system damage
hydroquinoneirritation and abnormal pigmentation
tretinoinredness, peeling, sensitivity
potent corticosteroidsskin thinning and pigmentation changes

Unregistered products may cause skin irritation, kidney damage or nervous-system damage（神經系統損害）.

5.4 Medicines and Cosmetics

Safe Cosmetic Choices

  • Buy registered products from reliable sellers.
  • Check the ingredient list and product information.
  • Avoid unrealistic claims（不實宣稱）.
  • Stop using a product if severe irritation occurs.
  • Seek professional advice when necessary.
5.5 Nanotechnology

5.5 Nanotechnology in Industry

5.5

Application of Nanotechnology

奈米科技的工業應用

1–100 nmgraphenesurface areaapplications
5.5 Nanotechnology

What Is Nanotechnology?

Nanotechnology is the development and application of materials, structures and devices approximately 1 to 100 nanometres（1 至 100 奈米） in size.
1 nm = 1 × 10−9 m

Nanomaterials may differ from the same material in bulk form（塊體形態） because they have a high surface-area-to-volume ratio（表面積與體積比） and many surface atoms.

5.5 Nanotechnology

Graphene Structure

5.5 Nanotechnology

Graphene Properties

  • very high tensile strength（抗拉強度）
  • low mass
  • flexibility and elasticity（彈性）
  • high thermal conductivity（導熱性）
  • high electrical conductivity and low resistance
  • high transparency
  • very low permeability（滲透性） to gases
5.5 Nanotechnology

Applications of Graphene

ApplicationRelevant Property
Flexible electronic displaysFlexible, transparent and electrically conductive
Lightweight compositesStrong and low in mass
Electronic componentsHigh conductivity and low resistance
Heat-management materialsHigh thermal conductivity
Sensitive sensorsHigh surface area; molecules adsorb（吸附）
Protective coatingsStrong and impermeable（不可滲透）
5.5 Nanotechnology

Other Nanotechnology Applications

  • TiO₂ and ZnO nanoparticles absorb or scatter ultraviolet radiation（紫外線） in sunscreen.
  • Silver nanoparticles are used in antimicrobial coatings（抗微生物塗層）.
  • Nanoparticles act as carriers（載體） for targeted medicine delivery.
  • Nanomaterials are used in smaller electronics and high-performance sensors.
  • Nanocoatings can be water-, scratch- or stain-resistant.
  • Nanomaterials strengthen composites（複合材料） without much extra mass.
5.5 Nanotechnology

Advantages and Concerns

Advantages / 優點
  • improved strength, conductivity or chemical activity
  • smaller and lighter products
  • efficient catalysts and sensors
  • targeted drug delivery（標靶藥物輸送）
  • reduced material use
Concerns / 疑慮
  • may enter cells or tissues
  • long-term effects not fully understood
  • difficult to recover from environment
  • testing, exposure control and regulation（監管） required
5.6 Green Technology

5.6 Green Technology

5.6

Industrial Waste Management

工業廢物管理中的綠色科技

electrolysisflocseffluentsludge
5.6 Green Technology

Green Technology

Green Technology develops products, equipment and systems that conserve（保護） the environment and natural resources while reducing negative impacts.
reduce pollution
minimise waste
conserve energy and raw materials（原料）
reuse / recycle
protect health and ecosystems（生態系統）
5.6 Green Technology

Industrial Wastewater

suspended solidsoilsdyesacidsalkalismetal ionsorganic pollutantsmicroorganisms

Industrial wastewater must be treated before discharge or reuse.

5.6 Green Technology

Electrocoagulation

Electrocoagulation is a wastewater-treatment process based on electrolysis（電解） using metal electrodes and a direct-current supply（直流電源）.
5.6 Green Technology

Electrode and Floc Reactions

Anode oxidationAl(s) → Al³⁺(aq) + 3e⁻
Cathode reduction2H₂O(l) + 2e⁻ → H₂(g) + 2OH⁻(aq)
Coagulant formationAl³⁺(aq) + 3OH⁻(aq) → Al(OH)₃(s)

Gelatinous Al(OH)₃ acts as a coagulant 混凝劑, adsorbing or trapping pollutants into larger flocs 絮凝物.

5.6 Green Technology

Main Stages of Electrocoagulation

  1. Current passes through the wastewater.
  2. The anode releases metal ions.
  3. Metal hydroxide coagulants（混凝劑） form.
  4. Pollutants are trapped in flocs.
  5. Flocs become sludge（污泥） and are separated.
  6. The treated effluent（處理後排放水） is tested.
5.6 Green Technology

Advantages of Electrocoagulation

  • Removes suspended particles, dyes, oils and some metal ions.
  • May require less chemical coagulant.
  • Can use compact equipment.
  • Produces flocs that are easy to separate.
  • May allow water to be reused or discharged more safely.
5.6 Green Technology

Responsible Sludge Management

Test before reuse
Sludge must be tested before reuse or disposal.
Hazardous sludge
Sludge containing toxic metals（有毒金屬） or hazardous chemicals must not be used directly in agriculture.
Beneficial use
Only sludge proven safe may be processed for beneficial use（有益用途）.

Why must sludge be analysed before agricultural use?

It may contain toxic metals or hazardous chemicals.

Experimental Design

variablesprocedureobservationssafety
Experiments

Experiment 1: Soap vs Detergent

TASK

Design an experiment to compare the effectiveness of soap and detergent in soft water and hard water.

KEYWORD BANKequal volumeequal concentrationsoft waterhard watersame shakinglather height
Problem: How does cleaning agent type affect lather in soft and hard water?
Hypothesis: Detergent produces more lather than soap in hard water.
MV: cleaning agent / water type. RV: lather height or persistence. CV: volumes, concentrations and shaking.
Experiments

Experiment 1: Procedure and Conclusion

Prepare equal volumes and concentrations of soap and detergent solutions.
Add equal volumes of soft or hard water to labelled test tubes.
Shake each tube using the same number and strength of shakes.
Measure lather height or time taken for lather to disappear.
Record observations in a table and compare.
Conclusion: detergent should produce more lather than soap in hard water.
Experiments

Experiment 2: Preparation of Soap

TASK

Describe a laboratory experiment to prepare soap from vegetable oil, including materials, procedure, functions, observations and safety.

KEYWORD BANKvegetable oilconcentrated NaOHheatstirsaturated NaClfilterwashdry
Heat vegetable oil with concentrated sodium hydroxide while stirring.
Add saturated sodium chloride, then cool.
Filter the solid soap, wash with cold water, press and dry.
Experiments

Experiment 2: Functions and Safety

NaOH: causes alkaline hydrolysis / saponification.
NaCl: lowers soap solubility and salts it out.
Observation: a solid soap layer / precipitate forms after salting out and cooling.
Wear goggles and gloves because NaOH is corrosive.
Use controlled heating / water bath and stir carefully.
Avoid splashing the hot alkaline mixture.
